title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Anthropic donates MCP to the new Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation
bullets.summary: MCP becomes a neutrally-governed project alongside Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md; Platinum backers AWS, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI; 10,000+ active public MCP servers.
bullets.how: Governs The Construct's entire MCP fleet; neutral stewardship de-risks our all-in MCP bet and pairs with the 07-28 spec RC — treat protocol evolution as planned standards-body maintenance and keep our integration layer spec-current.

bullets.title: OpenAI closes record $122B round at ~$852B post-money; Anthropic's ~$965B Series H now exceeds it; both filed confidentially for IPOs
bullets.summary: Amazon, NVIDIA, SoftBank and a16z anchor OpenAI's raise; frontier capital keeps compounding.
bullets.how: Validates the agent-operator thesis but raises the competitive bar; keep a build-vs-buy read on frontier models and lean into the SMB/mid-market operator tier these platforms won't serve directly.

bullets.title: Capital floods the long-running-agent infra layer — Sail Research $80M ($450M val); Baseten $1.5B Series F
bullets.summary: Investors funding the durable-autonomy substrate for agents that run hours-to-days ('run models, not build them').
bullets.how: Exactly the multi-hour/multi-day autonomy layer The Construct's harness depends on; cheaper long-run inference directly enables our Fable/Opus long-autonomy tiers — track as a cost lever for scheduled scans and agent loops.

bullets.title: Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro expected in July with advanced coding/agentic capabilities; Google in government talks
bullets.summary: After missing its June I/O date, Google positions Gemini 3.5 Pro as a coding/agent contender.
bullets.how: A live build-vs-buy and model-tiering option for coding-heavy Construct work; benchmark against Sonnet 5 before committing routing.

bullets.title: Anthropic in custom-silicon talks with Samsung to reduce Nvidia dependence
bullets.summary: A supply-chain move to bend the long-run inference cost curve as the paid base grows.
bullets.how: Downward pressure on inference cost improves the economics of running Sonnet 5 at volume while reserving Fable/Opus for long autonomy — a tailwind for our tiering strategy, not an action item.

praxis_lesson: The integration substrate just became shared industry infrastructure — donating MCP to a neutral Linux Foundation body makes the protocol a commodity standard, not a vendor asset, which de-risks our MCP bet but confirms the durable moat sits one layer up in the harness (orchestration, verification, memory tiers, scheduled scans). Meanwhile fresh capital is pouring into the long-running-agent infra layer where our multi-hour autonomy lives. Stay integration-agnostic on the now-commoditized protocol and concentrate investment in the orchestration + verification loop nothing commoditizes for us.
